source_admission: Published values cited in README.md and run.py, with how far each was read for this screening on 2026-10-17. The study's own numbers are arithmetic on the project's committed products; these sources give Earth's responses (cirrus thinning, methane's warmth, surface albedo) and two reference constants. No outside dataset or full paper is committed. Lenton & Vaughan 2009 is open access (CC BY 3.0) and was read in its methods and Table 1; the others were read at abstract or summary level as stated.

sources.citation: Lee JY, Marotzke J, et al. 2021, Future Global Climate: Scenario-Based Projections and Near-Term Information, Chapter 4 of Climate Change 2021: The Physical Science Basis (IPCC AR6 WG1), section 4.6.3.3
sources.use: README, the high cloud: Earth's cirrus warm the planet by about 5 W/m2 on net; cirrus thinning could take at most about 1-2 W/m2, with low confidence, and overseeding could warm
sources.access: known from the assessment as quoted in secondary summaries (search results of 2026-10-17); the chapter was not re-read for this study

sources.citation: Forster P, Storelvmo T, et al. 2021, The Earth's Energy Budget, Climate Feedbacks, and Climate Sensitivity, Chapter 7 of IPCC AR6 WG1
sources.use: run.py AR6_ERF_2XCO2: the effective radiative forcing of doubled CO2, 3.93 W/m2, set against the Earth control's own per-doubling change to carry the Moon's clear-sky CO2 forcing to all-sky
sources.access: a standard value of the assessment, known from it; not re-read

sources.citation: Mitchell DL, Finnegan W 2009, Modification of cirrus clouds to reduce global warming, Environmental Research Letters 4, 045102
sources.use: README table: the first estimate of cirrus seeding, a net cloud forcing more negative than -2.8 W/m2, delivered by airliners

sources.citation: Storelvmo T, Kristjansson JE, Muri H, Pfeffer M, Barahona D, Nenes A 2013, Cirrus cloud seeding has potential to cool climate, Geophysical Research Letters 40, 178-182
sources.use: README table: net cloud forcing down to -2.0 W/m2 at an optimal seeding concentration, with warming from too many ice nuclei
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results; not read in full

sources.citation: Muri H, Kristjansson JE, Storelvmo T, Pfeffer MA 2014, The climatic effects of modifying cirrus clouds in a climate engineering framework, Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
sources.use: README table: ice falling twice as fast, -1.55 W/m2 and -0.94 K globally
sources.access: values as a summary page (climateinterventions.org) quotes the paper; the publisher's page was not reachable

sources.citation: Gasparini B, Lohmann U 2016, Why cirrus cloud seeding cannot substantially cool the planet, Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
sources.use: README table: ECHAM-HAM's cirrus radiative effect 5.7 W/m2, with no seeding strategy giving significant cooling
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results

sources.citation: Gasparini B, McGraw Z, Storelvmo T, Lohmann U 2020, To what extent can cirrus cloud seeding counteract global warming?, Environmental Research Letters 15, 054002
sources.use: README table and run.py INP_PER_LITRE: favourable seeding gives -0.8 W/m2 in ECHAM (1 particle a litre, at night only) and -1.8 W/m2 in CESM (18 a litre); seeding reduced the CO2 rise in precipitation

sources.citation: Liu J, Shi X 2021, Estimating the potential cooling effect of cirrus thinning achieved via the seeding approach, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 21, 10609
sources.use: README table: CAM5 with seeding set by local conditions, -1.36 W/m2, -2.0 W/m2 kept out of low latitudes, where seeding warmed; fixed seeding at 20 and 200 a litre gave -0.27 and +0.35 W/m2

sources.citation: Penner JE, Zhou C, Liu X 2015, Can cirrus cloud seeding be used for geoengineering?, Geophysical Research Letters 42, 8777-8782
sources.use: README table: a net cooling of -0.74 W/m2 only with subgrid updrafts below 0.2 m/s and no deposition on existing ice during nucleation
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results

sources.citation: Tully C, Neubauer D, Omanovic N, Lohmann U 2022, Cirrus cloud thinning using a more physically based ice microphysics scheme in the ECHAM-HAM general circulation model, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 22, 11455
sources.use: README table and run.py CCT_OVERSEEDING_W_M2: no significant cooling except -0.36 W/m2 at 1 particle a litre, warming up to 4.9 W/m2 from overseeding at the highest concentration; cirrus thinning unlikely to be feasible globally

sources.citation: Kristjansson JE, Muri H, Schmidt H 2015, The hydrological cycle response to cirrus cloud thinning, Geophysical Research Letters 42, 10807-10815
sources.use: README: cirrus thinning avoids the weakening of the water cycle that solar dimming brings
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results

sources.citation: Yvon-Durocher G et al. 2014, Methane fluxes show consistent temperature dependence across microbial to ecosystem scales, Nature 507, 488-491
sources.use: run.py METHANOGENESIS_EV: methane emissions' average temperature dependence of 0.96 eV, a 57-fold rise from 0 to 30 C, applied between the targets' sea medians as an upper-end indicator
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results; the 57-fold rise from 0 to 30 C reproduced from 0.96 eV

sources.citation: Lenton TM, Vaughan NE 2009, The radiative forcing potential of different climate geoengineering options, Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics 9, 5539-5561
sources.use: run.py EARTH_F_A and the README: the two-way transmittance for surface albedo, 0.73 under a clear sky and about 0.48 over land with clouds; Table 1's land options (desert 0.44 brighter over 2% of Earth -2.12 W/m2; settlements 0.15 brighter -0.15 W/m2; urban areas 0.1 brighter -0.047 W/m2)
sources.access: open access; abstract, section 2.1 (equations 1-5) and Table 1 read

sources.use: run.py CITY_ALBEDO_RISE: roofs and pavements of urban areas raised by 0.1
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results

sources.citation: Irvine PJ, Ridgwell AJ, Lunt DJ 2011, Climatic effects of surface albedo geoengineering, Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
sources.use: README: desert brightening reduces precipitation over land by 3.9% per kelvin of cooling against 1.0% for a sunshade, and weakens the Indian and African monsoons
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results

sources.citation: Oleson KW, Bonan GB, Feddema J 2010, Effects of white roofs on urban temperature in a global climate model, Geophysical Research Letters
sources.use: README: white roofs everywhere cut the annual urban heat island by 33%, the daily maximum by 0.6 C and the minimum by 0.3 C
sources.access: abstract as summarized in search results
